The $6.8 billion iShares MSCI India ETF drew more than $316 million in fresh cash, its biggest weekly inflow since June 2025. Investors yanked $655 million from the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF — the most on record — last week, as well as $208 million from the iShares MSCI South Korea ETF as the rout deepened. Indian stocks have rallied 11% in dollar terms this month, outperforming the broader MSCI Emerging Markets Index , which is down 3.6% over the same period as technology shares in markets including Taiwan and South Korea tumble. ANI Market regulator Sebi has set up a sub-group under its Primary Market Advisory Committee (PMAC), headed by NSE chief Ashishkumar Chauhan , to review IPO and fundraising norms to simplify rules, reduce compliance burden and facilitate easier access to capital markets . The sub-group will review several Chapters of the ICDR Regulations . The review will cover eligibility conditions for various modes of capital raising, including initial public offerings (IPOs), follow-on public offerings (FPOs), preferential issues and qualified institutional placements (QIPs), Sebi said in a statement on Monday. It will also examine promoter and pre-issue capital lock-in requirements, application and allotment mechanisms, disclosure norms, pricing and price discovery frameworks, and due diligence requirements. "The review aims to identify opportunities to facilitate ease of access to the capital market for eligible issuers, simplify and rationalise regulatory requirements, eliminate duplicative disclosures and procedures, and improve regulatory clarity and consistency, while maintaining adequate disclosures, investor protection and market integrity," the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) said. Live Events The panel will also review relevant Sebi circulars, advisories and other regulatory directions to identify areas requiring consolidation, modification or alignment with the ICDR Regulations. It will review and rationalise disclosure requirements applicable to IPOs, FPOs, preferential issues and QIPs, including disclosures in offer documents. The panel will also review pricing requirements and the applicable price discovery framework, including determination and disclosure of the price or price band, floor price as applicable to the respective modes of capital raising. Reuters India's investment in US Treasury securities increased USD 38.4 billion, or 21 per cent, between June and August, coinciding with substantial inflows of Foreign Currency Non-Resident (FCNR) (B) deposits into the Indian banking system. According to data compiled by PTI from the US Department of the Treasury, India's investment in US Treasuries rose to USD 219.7 billion in August 2026 from USD 181.3 billion in May 2026, just before the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) introduced the concessional facility. Gaura Sengupta, economist at IDFC First Bank , said the RBI's foreign exchange reserves increased during the period of FCNR(B) inflows, with a portion of the accretion being invested in US Treasury securities. The RBI had introduced a special USD-INR swap facility on June 8, 2026, to encourage foreign currency inflows and strengthen the country's balance of payments position. The facility allowed banks to mobilise fresh FCNR(B) deposits with maturities of three to five years and swap the foreign currency with the central bank at concessional rates. Following the strong response, the RBI advanced the closure of the facility for fresh FCNR(B) deposits to August 31, 2026, from the earlier deadline of September 30. Live Events The facility mobilised USD 127.23 billion through FCNR(B) deposits by August 31, while total inflows, including overseas foreign currency borrowings and external commercial borrowings, stood at USD 136.38 billion, according to RBI data. The inflows helped the central bank mop up dollars from the market, shore up the country's foreign exchange reserves and provided room for investment in overseas assets, including bonds. India's foreign exchange reserves increased USD 58.572 billion between June and August. Reserves stood at USD 740.803 billion as of August 28, 2026, compared with USD 682.231 billion as of May 29, 2026. During the period, the yield on 10-year US Treasury securities rose to 4.75 per cent as of August 31, 2026, from 4.45 per cent as of May 29, 2026.
